reviews.reviewerContext: Independent Lens and companion-shell review subagent, 2026-11-22

composition.observation: The centered navy Lens dims the desktop Journal while keeping the book and objective bar recognizable. At 390 pixels the same bounded overlay fills most of the viewport.

hierarchy.observation: The named spatial moment and Voyage identify the dialog. A parchment panel makes the Captain's note and its clue distinguishable from browser AR availability and view instructions.

typography.observation: Serif scene and note titles distinguish the story from the sans-serif availability copy and action labels. The full clue wraps legibly across three lines at the mobile checkpoint.

spacing.observation: Desktop action buttons sit on one row. Mobile wraps Place in Guided View beneath Choose and Inspect. The note and local inspection response have padding and a divider, while secondary footer text extends below the visible crop.

controls.observation: Choose, Inspect and Place in Guided View sit beside the clue, with a separate close button and a visibly disabled Start browser AR. Inspect changes the note area in the captured journey.

contrast.observation: The warm parchment carries dark clue text. Action buttons use light-on-navy lettering, and the high-contrast gold focus ring remains distinct from the dimmed page and subdued disabled AR control.

consistency.observation: Both widths and motion modes repeat the Voyage name, exact northern-light clue, action order and local inspection copy. The same objective remains visible after close.

states.observation: Journal tools appear before launch. Lens supplies an opening message, resolves to the released note, adds the inspection sentence and removes the overlay on return.

responsive.observation: Desktop keeps a centered modal and spread. Mobile shows a single Journal page and stacks the parchment controls inside the modal. Close, clue and inspection feedback are within the 390-pixel evidence.

keyboard.observation: Sampled frames show the close button focused at entry and focus moving to Choose or Inspect. The keyboard journey opens, inspects and closes while retaining the Journal content.

focus.observation: The gold ring is visible on the close control when Lens opens and on Open Chronicle Lens or Lens once the dialog closes on both widths.

feedback.observation: Inspect adds an immediate description of the parchment in all variants, and desktop also exposes the recorded-interaction footer. The captured first visible feedback measures about 104 to 211 ms.

motion.observation: Normal Journal entry animates and then shows an opening recovery notice. Reduced uses the readable page-turn fallback. Both traces present the same stable clue, inspection and direct close destination within the interaction budget.

continuity.observation: The Voyage title persists on the dialog and Follow the lanterns is present before and after. Capture continuity reports matching Voyage and edition fingerprints at the visible outcomes and after return for all four variants.

complexity.observation: The single dialog gives the clue without another setup step. The three verbs share one note panel and the visibly explained camera restriction has no effect on inspecting or returning.

role-outcomes.observation: The signed-in Player receives the released text and gets a meaningful inspection result while the returned objective remains Follow the lanterns. The capture's role and return checks pass for every reviewed mode.

fallbacks.observation: The disabled browser AR button explains that world tracking is unavailable here, while Guided View supplies the northern-light clue without a camera. Reduced Journal rendering still provides the passage and Continue Voyage.

findings.observation: The mobile Lens footer starts low and desktop's recorded-interaction footer is below the visible mobile inspected view. The parchment immediately displays its own inspection result and close remains visible.
Full-motion Journal frames explicitly report that the animated opening could not finish. The actual passage, Lens entry and return remain available.

limits: Synthetic authorized account and populated Voyage in the isolated desktop browser and 390 by 844 mobile browser emulation as applicable.
Reviewed browser captures establish the selected actions and visible states. Screen-reader output, physical hardware and independent user acceptance require separate evidence.

Only the published synthetic clue consumer and Guided View Inspect route were reviewed. Native camera, Creator authoring/publication, Choose and Place activation, and other accessibility paths were outside the observed journey.

reviews.reviewerContext: Independent Lens and companion-shell review subagent, 2026-11-22

composition.observation: The Journal companion is a centered reading column with a contextual header, while the Chronicle Library opens into a desktop navigation and filter bar. Return restores the book spread and bottom objective.

hierarchy.observation: Exit to My Voyages is visible above the companion context. The active Voyage identity and Journal companion heading orient the reader. The Library promotes its heading and Active Voyages to primary destinations.

typography.observation: Large serif headings distinguish the passage and Library from the sans-serif role, sync and filter labels. The reader also offers explicit A and A+ size controls.

spacing.observation: The companion has a bounded reading lane with space between its sync line, selector and parchment. The Library has room for inline Search, State and Sort, with the active card beginning below them.

controls.observation: Exit to My Voyages, shell Return and Return to Chronicle are separately visible. The trace follows the named exit and resumes the active Voyage through the Library. Continue Voyage appears in the returned Journal.

contrast.observation: Parchment and dark story type are clearly distinct from teal chrome. The Library focus ring and server-confirmed badge retain strong separation from the surrounding surface.

consistency.observation: The Voyagewright brand and identity affordance survive the player-to-library change, with consistent teal and parchment treatment. The same titled passage appears in both companion and returned Journal.

states.observation: The trace progresses through device access checks and Journal companion readiness, through server-confirmed Library and opening Journal, to the readable passage with a current-objective bar.

responsive.observation: At 1440 by 900 the compact companion header and wide Library filters fit without horizontal crowding. The normal return frames the spread and the reduced return frames the current page. Mobile is evaluated by its own contract.

keyboard.observation: The sequence shows visible skip and filter focus progression, the named contextual exit, movement to the active record and keyboard return to the Journal. The two related actions passed capture keyboard checks.

focus.observation: The Library heading gets a clear rectangular focus outline after the exit. Later samples show the focus ring moving to Sort and Active Voyages rather than staying on the departed view.

feedback.observation: Connection status, server confirmation and opening loader communicate progress. Reduced mode shows connection interruption and recovery while maintaining the passage. Measured initial response is about 108 to 127 ms.

motion.observation: Full motion briefly layers outgoing content and ends in a visible recovery notice. Reduced motion uses a readable page-turn fallback and reaches the same voyage passage. Both keep the primary actions available.

continuity.observation: The synthetic voyage name is shown in the companion and active Library record, and Follow the lanterns returns in both modes. The capture reports matching authorized-person fingerprints through exit and reopen.

complexity.observation: The contextual exit takes the Player directly to their Library, with one active record exposed. The real route passes through the Open the journal gate as a named, identifiable step.

role-outcomes.observation: The Player reaches their own server-confirmed Library, reopens the current adventure and can see Continue Voyage. Both capture modes verify the role and return path.

fallbacks.observation: The normal return explicitly recovers from the animated opening. The reduced return reports readable page turning, and both show the current passage and Continue Voyage.

findings.observation: Full-motion return shows a recovered opening and starts lower in the spread than the reduced checkpoint. The passage and Continue Voyage remain readable.

limits: Synthetic authorized account and populated Voyage in the isolated desktop browser and 390 by 844 mobile browser emulation as applicable.

composition.observation: A single-column companion keeps the shell, contextual link, sync and parchment in order. The Library replaces the companion header with compact public chrome and vertical filters. The Journal returns as one page with a bottom action shelf.

hierarchy.observation: Exit to My Voyages appears above the Voyage label and the full-width Return to Chronicle link. The Library heading leads its filters and the Active Voyages section, with the current objective prominent on return.

typography.observation: The Library title wraps across two legible lines within its visible focus box. The companion's serif title and short parchment paragraphs fit the column alongside clearly labeled form controls.

spacing.observation: The companion controls have reserve width and a full-width release selector. The Library filters fit with usable vertical gaps, but the active card is below the first fold. The fixed tabs and objective consume meaningful reading height in the returned book.

controls.observation: Shell Return, Exit to My Voyages, Return to Chronicle and reading-size controls remain distinct. Continue Voyage has a visible target and passes viewport hit testing and trial activation checks in both returned modes.

contrast.observation: Light headings and control text stand out against dark teal. The Library title focus ring is clear. The returned gold Continue Voyage button is visually separated from the red tabs and parchment.

consistency.observation: Both modes retain the Voyagewright account affordance and the same Journal companion structure. The returned Follow the lanterns objective and reduced-motion page use the same parchment language.

states.observation: The sampled journey exposes reconnect with Retry, the in-sync companion, server-confirmed Library, and the reopened current Journal. In reduced motion the post-return connection status visibly recovers.

responsive.observation: At 390 by 844 the companion aligns in one column, Library search and filters stack without horizontal overflow in the capture, and a scrolled normal Journal reveals Previous and Next above its fixed tabs.

keyboard.observation: The rendered trace shows focus changing from shell navigation through Library controls and the active voyage is reopened through the keyboard journey. Capture checks passed for the two scoped actions in both modes.

focus.observation: The Library's two-line heading is outlined on exit, and subsequent Gallery or List focus is visible within the viewport. The active journey returns without horizontal displacement.

feedback.observation: A Retry affordance accompanies the transient reconnect state, which settles to Same Voyage in sync. The Library displays Server confirmed. At return the reduced flow shows Connection restored. Measured initial feedback is about 81 to 101 ms.

motion.observation: Normal reentry briefly animates the opening and then presents a readable recovery. Reduced skips to the readable page-turn fallback, preserving the passage and bottom action without depending on the full ceremony.

continuity.observation: The same context starts in the companion, the capture confirms the same active voyage in the Library, and the final Journal still displays Follow the lanterns. Both modes report matching authorized-person fingerprints.

complexity.observation: The two return destinations are individually labeled. The one active Library record requires going below the stacked filters at this viewport, then the book offers the normal resume gate and current objective.

role-outcomes.observation: The signed-in Player exits to their own Library and returns to an actionable same-Voyage Journal. Capture role and return checks pass, including the unblocked Continue Voyage action.

fallbacks.observation: The companion offers Retry on reconnection, and the Journal presents explicit opening recovery in normal or readable page turning in reduced. Core passage and Continue Voyage remain available.

findings.observation: Stacked Library filters put the sole Active Voyages card below the first fold at 390 by 844. It remains reachable in the verified journey.

The fixed tabs and objective cover lower portions of the returning page at some scroll positions. The normal checkpoint shows Previous and Next above the fixed UI, and the primary Continue Voyage target remains visible and hit-testable in both modes.
The normal returning Journal shows the animated-opening recovery notice. Passage, page navigation and Continue Voyage remain present.

The selected shell exit and resume route was reviewed in an emulated viewport. Standard browser hit testing checks the captured Continue Voyage target, with physical touch ergonomics still unmeasured.

composition.observation: The dimmed Journal remains a recognizable backdrop to the centered pairing dialog. Normal desktop frames show the two-leaf spread and persistent objective bar when the modal closes.

hierarchy.observation: The pairing title and current Voyage lead the dialog, followed by the QR, same-account guidance, code alternative, and return action. The returned book reestablishes Follow the lanterns and its Continue Voyage action.

typography.observation: Serif reading titles distinguish the Chronicle from the small sans-serif operational controls. The phone modal wraps the Voyage name and instructions as whole words at 390px.

spacing.observation: The QR, instructions, and manual-code row have distinct vertical breathing room. In portrait, device rows push Continue the Chronicle below the initial panel fold, while Close stays visible.

controls.observation: Connect another device opens the contextual dialog. Continue the Chronicle dismisses it via the named control in both keyboard traces, and the paired transfer adds an explicit Cancel send on the originating Journal.

contrast.observation: The black QR on white and solid pale text on a dark panel are visually distinct. The visible gold focus border on the trigger and Close survives both narrow and wide layouts.

consistency.observation: The normal and reduced dialogs retain the same Voyage name, same-account guidance, QR/alternative order and pale-on-dark treatment. After pairing, the same dialog updates the connection state in place.

states.observation: The reduced trace shows Preparing your connection before the code. The adverse phone run rejects the stale code with a new-code remedy, then the paired phone reaches the in-sync Journal companion on successful retry.

responsive.observation: Desktop pairing is a bounded dialog over the two-leaf Journal. At 390px it uses a single-column panel and preserves the QR and code alternative, then returns to the single-page layout with the four tools and objective still visible.

keyboard.observation: The generic traces contain Tab traversal and Enter activation for Connect another device and Continue the Chronicle on each viewport size. The capture records keyboard pass for all four device/motion combinations.

focus.observation: The modal's Close control receives a visible ring on open. After dismissal the ring returns to Connect another device in both viewport families, preserving the keyboard user's place.

feedback.observation: The preparing label leads to scannable joining guidance. Capture measures 283–450 ms to the contracted visible feedback; the paired origin separately moves from ready to receive to open on the other device.

motion.observation: The paired normal desktop sequence shows the staged cover and seal and then the readable spread. Reduced lands on a readable single leaf and still presents pairing and return. The generic normal notice about animation fallback leaves the active text and actions available.

continuity.observation: The same Follow the lanterns objective and Journal tools are visible before and after connection. The captured Voyage and edition fingerprints agree across outcomes. The paired phone returns to that Chronicle and can reach Voyage complete.

complexity.observation: Pairing begins beside the reading task without an account-settings detour. Manual code is progressively disclosed while the paired recovery actions are grouped under Connected view options.

role-outcomes.observation: A signed-in Player opens the matching Voyage companion and its authored clue on the second screen. In adverse recovery the crew screen shows the read-only audience and receives the authorized passage/chart, while the private letter appears only on authorized personal return.

fallbacks.observation: The manual pairing route remains available alongside QR. The separate phone shows an offline released chart with Retry, later returns to in-sync, and the revoked current screen clears companion content and offers a safe return or retry.

findings.observation: At 390×844 the connection dialog still says to open your phone's camera and places Continue the Chronicle below the first viewport when device rows are present. The immediately visible Close and keyboard-accessible Continue both support the observed safe return.

The receiver consents to The island course and the sender acknowledges it by passage name, but the resulting purpose is Voyage Chart. Explicit receipt and continuity work; the acceptance copy leaves the resulting view type implicit.

limitations: Chromium and guarded synthetic account, persisted Voyage, and edition only. The paired run used isolated desktop and mobile browser contexts with virtual viewports, including a simulated offline condition.

Physical phone/QR scan, camera permission and native AR, physical network interruption, and screen readers were outside the inspected capture. Actual recordings were reviewed through meaningful Playwright trace screencast sequences. WebM was not separately played.
The measured feedback values are capture-reported timings for contracted keyboard transitions. They are not a physical-device performance benchmark or proof of every animation frame.

composition.observation: The companion centers a single reading/purpose surface with the Voyage and return context above. Portrait Lens rededicates that width to the clue and its three actions. Desktop purpose changes keep the same bounded panel.

hierarchy.observation: Purpose headings distinguish Journal companion, Voyage Chart, and Artifact viewer. The Chart objective sits before the map and the artifact name before its rendered image and description.

typography.observation: The passage, Captain's note, and letter use dark readable serif text on light paper. Controls and synchronization use sans-serif. The larger reading-size action is visible and reachable in the Journal trace.

spacing.observation: Purpose panels leave space between title, description, controls and their primary content at both widths. On the 844×390 landscape capture the two stacked global rows and context push the map below the first viewport, while Chart title and Return are still visible.

controls.observation: The purpose chooser separates common choices from More purposes; the artifact is reached there. The paired offer presents distinct Receive and Decline controls, and the private letter send requires the visible selected-device confirmation.

contrast.observation: Light-on-dark purpose titles and dark-on-parchment reading content remain clear. The active purpose heading gains a blue outline, while the unavailable browser AR control is muted and explained in readable text.

consistency.observation: Journal companion, Chart, and Artifact retain the same Voyage identity and same-voyage status pattern while rendering distinct purpose content. The corresponding narrow/reduced states preserve that order and destination.

states.observation: Connecting, in-sync, offline with the last released view, reconnected, and revoked are visually different. The shared screen begins with a deliberate-sharing empty state and only then displays the explicitly received read-only view.

responsive.observation: At 390px portrait the Journal, clue, chart and artifact each fit the single content column; at 844×390 the heading and return remain legible. The medium-width main Chronicle keeps the book and objective available while the narrow companion remains independent.

keyboard.observation: Tab/Enter events traverse purpose change, Lens close, Chart, More purposes, artifact, Journal, larger reading size and Return to Chronicle on desktop and mobile. Capture records keyboard pass in all four runs.

focus.observation: On changing purpose, the framed Chart, Artifact viewer, or Journal heading visibly identifies the destination. The Lens close has a high-visibility focus ring and the trace shows subsequent traversal to the reading-size control.

feedback.observation: Capture records 91–154 ms from the measured keyboard action to visible purpose feedback. Paired recovery shows updating connected screens and then devices up to date, and the phone states visibly change between offline and in sync.

motion.observation: Purpose content and each return remain available in both preferences. The paired normal desktop renders a staged book opening, while reduced reaches the single readable leaf without that staged ceremony; both phone paths eventually show Voyage complete.

continuity.observation: The restored companion shows the same released Follow the lanterns prose. Return reopens the same active Chronicle; paired evidence additionally shows the originating book left in place during receipt and the authorized personal return restoring the selected letter.

complexity.observation: Common companion purposes sit in an explicit chooser, with additional choices behind More purposes. Guided Lens gives direct actions for the note, and the busy map/offline options can stay collapsed while reading.

role-outcomes.observation: The guided Lens renders the actual clue and its inspection state, Voyage Chart presents Secret Isle as the current objective, Artifact viewer shows the released brass compass, and Journal displays the released prose and letter. Revocation removes private content from the current companion.

fallbacks.observation: The Lens explains that browser world tracking is unavailable and retains the same Captain clue in Guided View. Offline Chart remains readable with Retry. The adverse trace shows private send and crew paths without a camera or gesture dependency.

findings.observation: At the rotated 844×390 phone viewport, repeated shell/context rows leave only the Chart heading above the fold. Return and synchronization are visible and the capture preserves the chart role, but the dedicated map needs vertical travel.

The reviewed synthetic chart uses a line and square, and the released compass uses a star on a parchment-like panel. Titles, prose and objective carry the meaning in this fixture, so the review does not generalize the art impression to a full authored edition.
